p0.finding: Both HRM-005 aliases bypass the intended owner PEP because the People registry is v42, does not claim /v1/hris/organizations/graph and lacks the predicate and purpose closure.
All three PAY-013 routes are outside the v41 calculation and v48 Foundation PEPs; the prepare action additionally requires the v49 prepare predicate and a cryptographic step-up verifier seam.
All three SYS-002 routes are outside the v47 Platform HCM claim set, and generic Platform permission checks do not enforce the exact predicate, purpose and responsibility tuple.
All eight TIM-007 routes lack a close-owned v49 PEP; existing Time GatewayVerified implementations are unrelated feature-local patterns.
The settings purpose and exact Time per-route purpose assignments are not fully sealed in the final module decisions and must be bound by fresh amended tokens before source authoring.

The existing owner packets do not allocate every required shared security source and test path, so current-token source implementation is unauthorized even where a module wildcard could contain new files.

p1.finding: A full People registry move from v42 to v49 introduces six route contracts: operations home, organization graph, organization positions, performance goal cycles, time leave operations and team leave. Exact regression must prevent unreviewed semantic expansion.
The population PAGE and DATA routes have identical method and paths. Any path-only selector is ambiguous and must be rejected in favor of the trusted route key.
A duplicate preparation-local step-up cryptographic implementation would create policy drift; the fresh token must allocate only a narrow visibility seam to the existing PayrollStepUpVerifier.
The Platform registry must claim encoded and structural near-misses in the three new path families so they are denied instead of falling through to generic authorization.
Only close and reopen have v49 step-up command bindings; applying a fresh challenge to validate or handoff, or omitting it from close or reopen, would contradict the sealed transport semantics.
Default-OFF and tenant-unenrolled tests must prove zero business bean, controller, service, repository, outbox and worker calls; a rendered denial or empty response alone is insufficient.
